title: Sent Out to Fill the Earth

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Bring out every kind of living creature that is with you - the birds, the animals, and all the creatures that move along the ground - so they can multiply on the earth and be fruitful and increase in number on it." So Noah came out, together with his sons and his wife and his sons' wives. - Gen 8:17-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As Noah steps out into a cleansed world, God gives a familiar command: "be fruitful and increase in number." These were the very words God spoke to Adam and Eve at creation (Gen 1:28). Now, on the far side of the flood, God renews His purpose for life to fill and flourish on the earth. It is a fresh start - a new beginning for creation, with Noah as a kind of second Adam.

What grace this is! God does not abandon His good purposes because of human sin. The flood was real judgement, but it was not the end of God's plan. He brings His people through it into a renewed world and says, in effect, "Begin again. Let life flourish. My purposes stand."

This is the hope woven through all of Scripture. Human sin does not get the last word; God's purpose of blessing and life does. Again and again, God brings His people through judgement into new beginnings, through death into resurrection.

We serve a God of fresh starts. Whatever floods have swept through your life, God is able to bring you out into new ground and say, "Begin again." And this new beginning points forward to the greatest one of all - the new creation Christ is bringing, where life flourishes forever under God's blessing (Rev 21:5). The One who brought Noah into a renewed world will bring His people into a world made new.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you believe God can give you a genuine fresh start?
- How does the hope of a renewed creation encourage you today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: God of new beginnings, thank You that sin does not get the last word - Your purpose of life and blessing does. Bring me out into new ground, and thank You for the new creation Christ is bringing.
